definitions.definition: For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
Notation in this copied formula: H_tau=Htau at timestep tau, F_tau=Ftau, P_0=P0, D^(-1)=Dinv and D^(-2)=(Dinv)^2=Dinv2; S_r is the group S at time r. The bracket variable G denotes the entire expression depending on s inside that bracket.

definitions.type: unmodified time-step map and finite numerical trajectories
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f), tau>0. For a positive integer Lsteps and tau=T/Lsteps, set t_n=n*tau and u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n), 0<=n<Lsteps; v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. No spatial frequency cutoff is applied. This is a finite recursion; its L^2 continuity and preservation properties are proved below.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). Interp_(a,tau;f) denotes this entire tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y). It is just these formulas, with no error estimates or endpoint matching granted.

inputs.statement: For tau>0, n>=0 integer, t_n=n*tau and a smooth real mean-zero f, let uold=S_(t_n)f and unew=Psi_tau(uold), with the displayed unfiltered update. Then S_(-(t_n+tau))unew=f+Fstage_(t_n,t_n+tau)(f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Fstage_(t_n,s)(f)) ds-Rem_(t_n,tau)(f,f,f). The Rem is exactly the covariance eta and multiplier in D015, with zero output mode. This is an exact identity without a consistency error, frequency cutoff or convergence premise.
source_conditions: tau>0 and n is a nonnegative integer.
f is spatially smooth, real and mean-zero, and the physical update is precisely (1.4).

inputs.statement: The following estimates have constants uniform in the real time t. For mean-zero f in L^2, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2. For any A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). For f,g in L^2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0 with Dinv A0 in L^2 and g in L^2, ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2 and ||J_t(A0,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2. For smooth mean-zero time-dependent f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=Ctri_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise and sum across internal endpoints for continuous piecewise smooth paths. For time-independent mean-zero f,g, Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t). The bounded products extend from polynomials by density.

output.statement: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is a continuous map on the real mean-zero L^2 space, preserves mean zero and reality, and maps smooth data to smooth data; Ftau:L^2->H^1 is continuous. Hence all finite numerical trajectories are defined and continuous in the initial datum. For every smooth mean-zero real f, tau>0 and integer n>=0, S_(-(n+1)*tau)Psi_tau(S_(n*tau)f)=f+Fstage_(n*tau,(n+1)*tau)(f)+integral_(n*tau)^((n+1)*tau)B_s(f,Fstage_(n*tau,s)(f))ds-Rem_(n*tau,tau)(f,f,f). Consequently on a numerical smooth trajectory the tuple Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n) has Vst(t_n)=v^n and Vst(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1). The interpolants therefore concatenate to a continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero real V on [0,T].

argument.text: Fix tau>0. N005 makes Dinv:L^2->H^1 bounded and H^1 an algebra. Therefore Ftau is a continuous quadratic map L^2->H^1. In Htau the first product has factors S_tau Dinv f and Dinv Ftau(f) in H^1; the second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2) and S_tau Dinv f; the third is an H^1 cube followed by Dinv and S; the fourth multiplies S_(s-tau)Dinv2 Ftau(f) by S_s Dinv f in H^1, followed by Dinv2 and S, evaluated at two endpoints. Every coefficient, including 1/tau, is finite at this fixed tau. Hence all four terms, Ftau and Psi_tau are continuous in L^2. Fourier conjugate symmetry is preserved by S, Dinv, products and real coefficients. Every projected or inverse-derivative term has zero mean, and the unprojected second term of Htau is a scalar times the mean-zero S_tau Dinv f. Thus the update is real and mean-zero. The same formulas preserve spatial smoothness. Finite induction gives the asserted well-defined finite trajectories and continuous dependence at fixed tau.

produces.statement: For each fixed tau>0 the full update Psi_tau is continuous on real mean-zero L^2, preserves that subspace and smoothness, and Ftau maps continuously to H^1.

argument.text: For the endpoint identity now take smooth real mean-zero f and integer n>=0. Apply E006 with precisely this f,n,tau. Its exponential convention agrees with S_(-t), and its F^n and A^n are respectively Fstage and the displayed B integral; its R_2^n is D015 with t0=n*tau. This gives exactly the asserted twisted update. There is no norm conversion in this algebraic identity.

produces.statement: The exact twisted update displayed in the output assertion holds for every smooth real mean-zero f,n,tau.

argument.text: At t=t_n, all stage integrals in Interp vanish and its affine correction is zero, so Vst(t_n)=f. At t=t_n+tau, Q(t) cancels its contribution to W and Vst=f+Fstage+Cst-Rem. With f=v^n, F002 identifies this as v^(n+1). F001 ensures the next state remains smooth and real mean-zero. Thus adjacent pieces have matching endpoints, and the concatenation is continuous and piecewise smooth, real and mean-zero. This proves the output assertion.
